draft.title: Correlation and causation
card: Correlation means two variables move together. Causation means a change in one variable produces a change in the other.
A strong correlation does not prove causation. The data only shows that the variables move together, not why.
a separate variable that affects both of the others and makes them move together. Ice cream sales and sunburn cases both rise in hot weather, so temperature is a third factor.
To claim causation, there needs to be more than a scatterplot or a value of r. A reasonable explanation for how one variable affects the other is needed, and third factors need to be ruled out.
draft.remember: Moving together does not prove one causes the other. Look for a third factor.

a.q: A town finds a strong positive correlation between the number of fire trucks sent to a fire and the damage done. What is the best conclusion?
opts: The correlation alone does not show trucks cause damage
Sending more fire trucks causes more damage to buildings
Damage causes fewer fire trucks to be sent to a fire
The correlation is an error, as r cannot be positive here
a.why: A correlation shows only that the variables move together. A third factor, the size of the fire, probably leads to both more trucks and more damage. Saying the trucks cause the damage is the tempting mistake.
a.clue: Think about what makes both numbers larger.

b.q: Data from a city shows that suburbs with more swimming pools have more cases of heat stroke. Which is the most likely reason?
opts: Hotter suburbs have more pools and more heat stroke
Owning a pool causes heat stroke in the owner
Heat stroke leads people to build pools at home
Pools and heat stroke are unrelated, so r must be 0
b.why: Hot weather is a third factor that could lead to both more pools and more heat stroke. Claiming pools cause heat stroke treats the correlation as causation. The data show the variables move together, so r is not 0.
b.clue: Look for a separate factor that affects both variables.

a.best: The correlation alone does not show trucks cause damage

b.best: Hotter suburbs have more pools and more heat stroke
